title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
author: Zora Neale Hurston
summary: Janie returns to her Florida town and tells her friend about her three marriages and her search for a life of her own. The story is told in rich dialect and with a strong sense of nature.
readIf: you like lyrical, voice-driven novels about independence, love and finding your own way of speaking.
skipIf: you find dialect hard to read; it takes a few pages to settle into the rhythm.

pairings.reason: Another story about a Black woman finding strength, voice and love in the early-twentieth-century South.
A more haunting and difficult novel that shares a rich, poetic voice and a woman's fight to own her life.
Another Southern classic with a vivid sense of community, told from a different place and angle.
